title: Adaptive phase-merging scheduler for latency-sensitive serving
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an adaptive phase-merging policy that dynamically decides when to merge prefill and decode micro-phases (or keep them split) based on per-request latency budget, kernel selection hints, and current GPU contention. Goal: reduce p95/p99 latency for interactive chat workloads while preserving overall throughput and fairness across customers.
motivation: Some workloads (short-turn chat, instruction-following) suffer from tail latency when aggressive batching or phase-splitting defers prefill work. Splitting phases improves throughput by enabling overlapping kernels but can increase end-to-end latency for small requests. We need a runtime policy that optimizes for observed latency budgets and hardware kernel characteristics at request time.
success_metrics: Reduce p95 latency for 1-8 token replies by >= 20% in hosted-chat traffic (measured on canary cluster)
Limit aggregate throughput regression to < 8% for mixed workloads compared to baseline
No increase in request-level fairness skew (Jain index delta < 0.02) across tenants
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive phase-merging toggle implemented and controllable via route policy
Integration tests covering merge/no-merge decisions under synthetic load
Canary rollout demonstrates target p95 improvement and acceptable throughput tradeoff
Observability: per-request decision tag, kernel hints emitted, and rollout dashboard added
rollout_plan: Stage 1: run in dry-run mode for 1 week on 10% of traffic, collect decision metrics
Stage 2: enable on non-critical routes (internal sandbox) and watch p95/p99
Stage 3: canary to 5% of production tenants for 72h
Stage 4: gradual ramp to 50% with automated rollback if SLO regressions detected
test_plan: Unit tests for decision logic (latency budget + kernel hint evaluation)
Integration test combining kernel selector and scheduler in CI harness
Load test scenarios: small-chat (avg 6 tokens), long-generation (avg 512 tokens), mixed-multi-tenant
A/B comparison against baseline scheduler using production-like traces
technical_notes: Decision inputs: request latency_budget, route SLA tier, model sequence length estimate, attention-kernel-cost-estimate
Heuristic: merge if latency_budget < threshold OR token_count_estimate <= small_request_threshold
Use kernel-selection feedback: if selected kernel has high prefill overhead (context-switch cost), merging may be better
Introduce 'merge_score' computed as weighted sum of latency_sensitivity, kernel_prefill_penalty, queued_prefill_time_estimate
Fairness: add proportional-share scaling to merge_score to prevent single-tenant starvation
Hedging: allow speculative merge for requests that exceed soft waiting deadline, with cancelation of redundant work if another path completes
alternatives_considered: Always-split phases: best for throughput but poor small-request tail latency
Static-route-level config: simple but requires per-route tuning and doesn't adapt to GPU congestion
Centralized RL-based policy: promising but high implementation cost and slow to converge; deferred for future work
